Filter Several Score-Driven Terms as One Recursion

Source: R/gas_joint.R
gas_joint.Rd

Checks that a set of built gas() terms can be filtered together and returns them as a GasJoint() object, with the cross loadings that each term's p_cross declares added to its parameters.

Usage

gas_joint(terms, drivers = character(0))

Arguments

terms

A named list of built GasTerm() objects, named by the distribution parameter in whose equation each one sits.

drivers

The names of the distribution parameters without a gas() term whose scores the terms load, or an empty vector. A fitting layer, which knows the family, checks that they are parameters of it.

Value

A GasJoint() object. Its terms are the input terms with cross_with filled, so their term_params() include the cross loadings, followed by one GasDriver() per entry of drivers; its params are the names of both.

Details

The terms must walk the same series: their by and time must give the same groups and the same order, because each score is read at the predictors of every equation at the same time. A term may develop its level, its loadings, its persistence or its cross loadings with a subformula.

The terms must share one scaling, because the driving vector is scaled by a power of the expected information of all the filtered parameters together. With more than one term the power is 0, 1/2 or 1: for these the derivatives of the matrix power are exact and short (the identity, the symmetric square root through a Sylvester equation per order, and the inverse).

The p_cross of a term names the parameters whose scores its level loads besides its own, with the number of lags of each. A parameter that it names with a positive count must be one of the joined terms or one of drivers, and a term cannot name its own parameter, whose score it loads through its own loadings. The cross loadings of a term follow the parameters in the order of the joined terms and then of drivers, lag by lag.

A parameter in drivers has no level of its own: its predictor is static, and its score enters the driving vector so that the levels of the terms can load it. It is carried as a GasDriver() member after the terms, with no parameters and a level of zero, which is a score-driven term whose loadings and persistence are zero. With a scaling other than zero the driving vector is scaled by the expected information of the filtered parameters and the drivers together.

See also

GasJoint(), gas()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(t = 1:40, y = rnorm(40))
tm <- list(mu = term_build(gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t,
                               p_cross = c(sigma = 2)), dd),
           sigma = term_build(gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t), dd),
           nu = term_build(gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t), dd))
jt <- gas_joint(tm)
lapply(jt@terms, term_params)
#> $mu
#> [1] "omega"        "kappa1"       "pacf1"        "kappa1_sigma" "kappa2_sigma"
#> 
#> $sigma
#> [1] "omega"  "kappa1" "pacf1" 
#> 
#> $nu
#> [1] "omega"  "kappa1" "pacf1" 
#> 

# The level of mu loads the score of sigma, whose predictor is static.
jd <- gas_joint(list(mu = term_build(gas(p = 1, q = 1, time = t,
                                         p_cross = c(sigma = 1)), dd)),
                drivers = "sigma")
jd@params
#> [1] "mu"    "sigma"
term_params(jd)
#> [1] "mu.omega"        "mu.kappa1"       "mu.pacf1"        "mu.kappa1_sigma"
